scope: same-instance initialize/close only, not append-close atomicity or production readiness

suggestions: The double-checked fast path in initialize() (`if self._conn is not None: return` outside the lock) is a benign optimization; combined with close() taking the same lock, the guarded path guarantees _conn is only published after schema+commit succeed and is never observed half-built, so serialized same-instance init/close holds.

close() correctly retains self._conn when commit() or close() raises (assignment to None only occurs after both succeed), so a commit/close failure propagates and cannot be read as a durable acknowledgement; the new tests cover commit-fail and close-fail paths.

contextlib.suppress(Exception) around the cleanup close() in initialize()'s error path does not catch asyncio.CancelledError (a BaseException); if cancellation lands during the cleanup await, the original error could be replaced by CancelledError. Consider catching BaseException (or explicitly CancelledError) in that suppress if cancellation during cleanup must never mask the root cause.
asyncio.Lock binds to the loop on first acquire (Python 3.10+); document/assume single-event-loop usage per instance, since reuse across separate asyncio.run loops would raise.

After a failed close() that leaves self._conn set, a subsequent initialize() no-ops via the fast path and will not reopen a possibly dead connection. This state/inconsistency pre-exists the diff and is not worsened, but a guard or a follow-up close-retry contract could be documented.
append()/query() still read _conn via _require_ready() without the lifecycle lock, so append-vs-close atomicity is unchanged (out of slice) — noted only that the new lock does not worsen it.

Minor test hygiene: tests/..test_concurrent_initialize_single_connection re-imports asyncio inside the function body; the monkeypatched execute gate keys on an exact SQL string, so future PRAGMA formatting changes could silently disable the gate.
review.summary: Bounded change adds a per-instance asyncio.Lock and wraps initialize() and close() bodies in it, with double-checked _conn publication and a suppressed cleanup close on the init error path. The lock serializes same-instance initialize/close so _conn is assigned only after connect, PRAGMAs, schema creation and commit all succeed; a racing close blocks on the lock and can never observe a partially published connection. close() commits then closes then clears _conn, so a commit or close failure propagates while leaving _conn intact, i.e. no false acknowledgement and no clearing of the live connection. Durable errors from initialize (e.g. schema failure) are re-raised after best-effort connection cleanup, and cancellation during init still routes through the BaseException handler to close the unpublished connection. No security regression and no new logic error identified; the pre-existing append-vs-close atomicity and pre-connect cancellation behaviors are unchanged and not worsened. Only non-blocking suggestions are offered. No tests were executed.
